cells.tense: You are right here at the door as something comes across, and your hand is already open.
cells.ask: Before it goes anywhere, write down in one line what just arrived and what you'll do with it, then do that today.
cells.core:
Something is arriving and you're present for it. Not bracing, not late — you're at the threshold when it crosses, and your hand is open. That catches more than it looks like. Most people only know what they're doing is good once it's answered back to them. You can feel it while it's still in your grip. You name it, you give it a shape, you don't wait for the form to prove itself first.

What this can feed next is itself, and support is how that happens. The resource in your hand gets stronger when it moves. You can hand that practical grip to someone else and still have it. So let it land somewhere. One line on what just came in, and one thing you'll do about it before the day ends, is the whole act.

cells.verb: taking a first form into the hand before anything is built on it
cells.place: at the moment something crosses the threshold and hasn't been absorbed yet

cells.tense: You have already named what it will become before it has arrived, and you are building the answer in advance.
cells.ask: Say what you think is coming, once, out loud — then do nothing about it for a day and see what stays true.
cells.core:
You're ahead of the door. Something hasn't crossed yet and you've already named it, shaped it, planned it — deciding what the seed will mean before it's in your hand. The energy isn't the problem; the timing is. You're spending this on arrivals that haven't happened and may not look like what you've prepared for.

It isn't less care in the planning that would help. Let knowing deepen instead of closing. You can't see what's actually arriving until it's here. If what you saw coming doesn't match what shows up, that's not failure — it's information your preparation couldn't have given you. So say one thing you think is coming, once, and let the day answer it.

cells.tense: You're still standing in a doorway that closed behind you, and what came through it never quite got taken in.
cells.ask: Pick one thing already to hand that you've been treating as not-arrived, and actually use it once today.
cells.core:
The door is right in front of you and your hand stayed down. Something was offered, or arrived, or was within reach, and it didn't get taken up. Opportunity isn't what's short here — the grip that would make it concrete is.

Don't try to reach for it out of an empty hand. Look at what's already here: the tool, the person, the thing you keep meaning to begin. Use one of them once, plainly, today. Starting from what's here is how the whole thing loosens. Then the same act gets easier — the first form is taken in, and something gets built on it instead of left standing at the door.

cells.tense: You are giving first form to the thing and calling it something that just turned up.
cells.ask: Name one thing you started as yours, out loud, and drop the word that had you crediting luck or timing for it.
cells.core:
You've been taking things in and giving them their first shape for a while now. The early form, the name you give it — it's yours, and you've been describing it as if it were happening to you. That's not modesty. It's the one place where saying 'I did this' would settle something.

You don't need volume to claim it. You already see it; what's left is saying it. Take one thing you started and call it that — 'I began this,' 'this one was mine from the start.' Simple, said once, to yourself first if that's where it has to land. What is here is yours to name, and saying so is how it gets to be built.

attempts.check: The record does not say what is actually arriving for this person — I render the seed and the timing but not its name, and any concrete noun I supply for the thing at the door would be invention. The reader could fairly say 'no — nothing is arriving that I didn't already have,' so every cell has to leave them the general truth, that the capacity to take something in and hold it is present, and only its exercise is in question. The asks all survive a wrong read: write the thing down once, clear one old thing out, let one arrival stay put, claim one thing already being done — each does work regardless of what is actually at the door. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'and that's the resource I'd say you've earned a claim on,' which follows from my read of their history and not from anything they can check.
